channel.title: The GW Hatchet - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The GW Hatchet (gwhatchet.com)

item.title: Staff editorial: Granberg’s vision is exciting. But at what price?
item.description: The strategic framework sounds great. But everything has a price, and it’s easy to support a vision before learning the trade-offs. The question is now, what will it take to bring Granberg’s vision to fruition?

item.title: Blood Orange blends alternative, R&B in front of sold-out District crowd
item.description: Devonté Hynes, known under the stage name Blood Orange, kicked off the second leg of his Essex Honey Tour at The Anthem Tuesday, bringing his quintessential blend of alternative pop and R&B to a sold-out crowd of more than 5,000 people.

item.title: Men’s basketball defeats St. Bonaventure 91-82 in overtime on Senior Night
item.description: Pregame, the team honored five student athletes as part of Senior Night honors, including star redshirt senior forward Rafael Castro who scored his 1,000th collegiate point in the game.

item.title: Faculty Senate preview: Lach to deliver annual presentation on key University metrics
item.description: The core indicators report, which is presented to the senate every year, states that GW's first-year retention rate dropped to its lowest level since 2021.

item.title: SGA calls for stronger free speech protections in revised Code of Student Conduct
item.description: Student Government Association senators unanimously passed a resolution Monday urging officials to bolster free speech protections in the Code of Student Conduct.

item.title: SBA fails to certify two Senate races after error excluded third-year students from voting
item.description: Senators voted Tuesday to reopen ballots for two at-large elections after the SBA’s elections director said graduating law students were mistakenly not allowed to vote in the elections.

item.title: GW hired consulting firm to develop Code of Student Conduct changes, which students say harm free speech
item.description: The Division of Student Affairs hired D. Stafford & Associates in spring 2025 to review and help revise GW’s Code of Student Conduct as students push back on proposed changes to the conduct process.

item.title: GWPD clears graduate workers union sit-in outside bargaining session
item.description: Roughly 30 graduate workers held a “grade-in” outside the negotiation room before officers asked them to leave the lobby.

item.title: Three GW students evacuated from Jordan following US-Israel strikes on Iran
item.description: Three students studying abroad in Jordan are evacuating the country, a University spokesperson confirmed, after the conflict descended upon the region in the wake of joint U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran since early Saturday.

item.title: Women’s basketball closes season with 62-54 tournament loss to Dayton
item.description: Women’s basketball dropped their first A-10 tournament matchup to Dayton 62-54, bringing their season to an end in Henrico, Virginia on Thursday.
